newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel holds key lending rate at 13.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel holds key lending rate at 13.9 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Sunday it was holding its key lending rate for April at an annualised 13.9 percent.
The rate is the one charged commercial banks at daily and weekly monetary tenders.
In a statement, the central bank attributed its decision to hold rates to accelerating inflation and money supply growth balanced by concerns about a slowing economy.

"On the one hand, the current inflationary environment and indices of inflationary developments for the future are at the upper end of the target," the central bank said. "In addition, the trend of growth in money supply is accelerating at a rate faster than desirable."
The government's 1997 inflation target is 7-10 percent.
"On the other hand, data pointing to a slowing in expansion of economic activity support the view that current monetary policy is consistent with inflationary targets," the central bank said.
Except for a pause in December, interest rates have been falling steadily since August by a total of 3.1 percentage points from a peak of 17 percent.
